_comment: Mutation survivors accepted as a baseline for the core sweep. The nightly ratchet fails when a survivor appears outside this set, and when an entry is no longer a survivor. Regenerate with `python scripts/mutation_gate.py --baseline core --update` after a sweep, and only ever let this set shrink. Entries are the survivor line without its line:col position, so they survive unrelated code motion.

_accepted.crates/valgebra-core/src/decision.rs: de: Every branch dropped is a refutation the arm names directly, and the goal reads it against its subject where it returns (`witnessed`). Deleting the arm hands the empty list to the general union rule as a union of no branches, which declines `A ⊆ ∅` for many a subject it cannot read: 561 of the 1,088 visits the core suite makes, each read on the longer route beside the arm's own answer. Every one is recovered further on by the same query: a narrowing by the cheap disjointness is the cheap disjointness of the whole union, which `unstructured` refutes on by construction, and one by the full reading is refuted by a reference's reduction or by the set representation the decision asks next. So no answer moves and the work does -- a decline where the arm refutes, then a second route to the same refutation -- and a test could see only the intermediate answer, which is a detail of the route rather than a claim of the relation.
_accepted.crates/valgebra-core/src/ir.rs: replace: An empty shared clause list against `Arc::default()`'s: the same value, and the same answers from every rule that reads it. Neither allocates -- std hands every empty `Arc<[T]>` of an alignment up to sixteen one static block, measured at no allocation for three defaults against one for `Arc::from([])` -- so the mutant reads one `OnceLock` fewer and costs nothing either way, an equivalent mutant on both counts. The function names the empty list at its call sites, and std documents the shared block as one it may give rather than one it must, where the interner compares a node's children by address (`ir/intern.rs`): the static is what makes every empty list one allocation by guarantee rather than by std's implementation.
The empty field list, on the same argument as `no_clauses`.
The empty member list -- a sequence shape with no fixed prefix -- on the same argument.
_accepted.crates/valgebra-core/src/kind.rs: replac: `Kind::NoneType`'s region is `1 << 0`, and `1 >> 0` is the same value. A genuinely equivalent mutant, and the only one of the seven shift constants that is: the other six are killed by `every_kind_lands_in_the_partition_and_the_scalars_land_apart`, which requires each scalar kind's region to be non-empty and pairwise disjoint and every container kind to share the one that is left.

`known` has one reader, the meet's emptiness rule (`intersection_verdict` in `decision/emptiness.rs`), and there it is an early answer the rule reaches again. A meet's region is known only where every member is a scalar-region term -- a keyed map, an attribute record, a refinement with a constraint and a class all read as unknown, and unknown absorbs -- so with the disjunct gone a known empty region passes the pair and bounds checks, which read no budget, and the map rule, which has no map to read, to `region.verdict()`, which answers `Empty`. The class branch before it needs an attribute record, so it never sees a known region. The mutant moves which line answers, not the answer or the steps: planted by hand, a record met with `int`, `(int | str) & (str | bytes) & (int | bytes)` and three more read the same verdict and the same `empty_steps`. It is kept for the instructions the early answer saves: deleted, the instruction gate's decision workloads count +0.25% (`--decision-repeat`), +0.11% (`--decision-rules`), +0.08% (`--decision-matrix`) and +0.03% (`--decision-refute`) more, the four rules it skips being run on every meet the scalar region empties.
